import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 883

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/883](https://www.erdosproblems.com/883)
- [ErSa97] Erdős, P. and Sárközy, G. N., On cycles in the coprime graph of integers.
  Electron. J. Combin. (1997), Research Paper 8.
- [Sa99] Sárközy, G. N., Complete tripartite subgraphs in the coprime graph of integers.
  Discrete Math. (1999), 227-238.
-/

open Filter

namespace Erdos883

/--
The coprime graph on $\mathbb{N}$: two integers are joined by an edge if they are coprime.
-/
def coprimeGraph : SimpleGraph ℕ :=
  SimpleGraph.fromRel Nat.Coprime

/--
For $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ let $G(A)$ be the graph with vertex set $A$, where two
integers are joined by an edge if they are coprime.

Is it true that if
$$|A| > \lfloor n/2 \rfloor + \lfloor n/3 \rfloor - \lfloor n/6 \rfloor$$
then $G(A)$ contains all odd cycles of length $\leq n/3 + 1$?

A problem of Erdős and Sárközy [ErSa97].
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_883.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (A : Finset ℕ),
      A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 n →
      n / 2 + n / 3 - n / 6 < A.card →
      ∀ l : ℕ, Odd l → 3 ≤ l → l ≤ n / 3 + 1 →
        l ∈ (coprimeGraph.induce (A : Set ℕ)).oddCycleLengths := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/--
Is it true that, for every $\ell\geq 1$, if $n$ is sufficiently large and
$$|A| > \lfloor n/2\rfloor + \lfloor n/3\rfloor - \lfloor n/6\rfloor$$
then $G(A)$ must contain a complete $(1,\ell,\ell)$ tripartite graph on $2\ell+1$ vertices?

The second question was solved by Sárközy [Sa99], who proved this with
$\ell \gg \log n/\log\log n$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_883.parts.ii : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ l : ℕ, 1 ≤ l → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ A : Finset ℕ,
      A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 n →
      n / 2 + n / 3 - n / 6 < A.card →
      (SimpleGraph.completeMultipartiteGraph (fun i : Fin 3 ↦ Fin (![1, l, l] i))).IsContained
        (coprimeGraph.induce (A : Set ℕ)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos883

reformulations.difference: The size threshold and cycle-length bound use natural-number arithmetic rather than the source's explicit floors and real quotient n/3.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For natural n, n / d equals floor(n/d). Moreover, n/6 ≤ n/2 + n/3, so natural subtraction does not truncate the threshold. For integer l, l ≤ floor(n/3)+1 is equivalent to (l : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ)/3+1. The complete RHS equivalence with integer floor expressions and the real-valued length bound was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean as Review883.partI_numeric_formulation_iff.

sources_consulted: Erdős–Sárközy, On cycles in the coprime graph of integers, Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 4(2) (1997), R8, especially §§1.1–1.2: https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/v4i2r8/pdf
Sárközy, Complete tripartite subgraphs in the coprime graph of integers, Discrete Mathematics 202 (1999), 227–238, especially pp.227–229: https://web.cs.wpi.edu/~gsarkozy/Cikkek/12.pdf
review.notes: Checked all three declarations; no mathematical defects or status discrepancies found. The live Erdős webpage was blocked, so I read archived copies through 30 August 2026 and the archived mathematical discussion, then corroborated the open status with the live public status dataset. Although ErSa97 discusses the optimal constant in a sufficiently-large-n theorem, the cited webpage explicitly poses the all-n version used in part (i). Part (ii) has the correct fixed-l, eventually-n quantifier order and positive answer. IsContained requires an injective, non-induced graph copy, correctly allowing additional edges within the three parts. Scratch proofs checked arithmetic equivalences, graph semantics, multipartite vertex counts, and boundary cases without sorry. Exhaustive testing of minimally admissible subsets for every n ≤ 21 found all requested odd cycles; larger admissible subsets inherit them.
